reason: The shovel at the workshop ground seems like a natural way to gather or prepare local material for paving.
expectation: I expect to dig or collect some local material, though I don't know exactly what the action produces.

alternatives.reason: The mesh and metal stock may make a useful screen, but I want to see what material the ground provides first.

effect: The shovel produced excavated regolith, giving me local material to work with.
reaction: That was a straightforward result; I’m curious how the regolith becomes paving.
reason: Making something from the mesh and metal stock is the only available combination, and it may produce a screen for the regolith.
expectation: I expect to make a screening tool, though I don’t yet know exactly how it will be used.

effect: The mesh and metal stock made a sieve, which can now be used on the excavated regolith.
reaction: The result makes physical sense, and I’m curious what the sieve separates out.
reason: Sieving the regolith is the only available combination and seems like a useful preparation for making paving.
expectation: I expect the sieve to separate the regolith by particle size, though I don’t know what material the game will produce.

effect: The sieve separated out large stones, leaving a more consistent feedstock for a furnace trial.
reaction: The explanation makes the sieving step feel useful; I’m curious how the material behaves when heated.
reason: The furnace trial is the only available combination and is the next step toward making paving.
expectation: I expect the furnace to heat the graded regolith into a solid material, though I’m unsure whether it will produce finished paving.

effect: The furnace produced porous bricks after a slower firing cycle, completing the paving goal and revealing that the workshop needs a solid floor.
reaction: The failed first trial and slower cycle made the firing feel like a useful experiment.
reason: Placing the fired bricks at the workshop ground seems like the direct way to make the new floor.
expectation: I expect to lay the bricks as a workshop floor, though I don't know whether more preparation will be needed.

alternatives.reason: The metal stock might help make a structure from the bricks, but the newly revealed floor goal seems more immediate.

effect: The bricks became workshop paving, completing the chapter. The level workbench shows how the floor makes the workshop more usable.
reaction: The detail about the bench staying put made the new floor feel tangible and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Firing the graded regolith was most worthwhile: the failed first trial and slower cycle showed how experimenting with heat produced usable porous bricks.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the sieve was straightforward but fairly predictable, especially as it was the only available combination.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the first firing flaked and that a slower cycle produced sound bricks.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear connection to preparing material or building the floor.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the practical details of making a workable floor were satisfying, and I’m curious how the expedition will build on it.
